findings.title: The second downsize definition replaces the existing API
findings.body: Ruby does not overload methods by argument signature: this definition replaces the preceding `downsize(from, to, max_width, max_height, opts={})` method. Existing callers supplying width, height, and options will now raise ArgumentError. Callers supplying only width and height will bind the height to `opts`, then fail when optimization accesses `opts[:allow_animation]`. Preserve both calling conventions in a single method or give the dimensions-string variant a separate name.

findings.title: Large animated GIFs lose their animation even when it is allowed
findings.body: The new downsizing call passes the upload's temporary path rather than its original filename. `OptimizedImage.optimize` selects animated processing only when the source path ends in `.gif`, but multipart upload tempfiles normally have no such extension. Consequently, even with `allow_animated_thumbnails` enabled, a large animated GIF is processed by the static ImageMagick instructions, which read only frame `[0]`. Because this operation overwrites the upload itself, the animation is permanently discarded before storage. Detect the image format independently of the tempfile extension or use a correctly suffixed temporary file.
